I have become all things to all people (1 Corinthians 9:22). Whom do I need to understand better?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us, as we have mercy on others.
interc: For the Church, that she may be patient and merciful.
For missionaries who live among other cultures, through St John de Britto.
For those we have judged harshly.
For the Church in Tamil Nadu.
For our group, that we may forgive and give in good measure.
pm.close: Father, you are patient with us and want all to be saved. Make us merciful as you are merciful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ezekiel saw dry bones rise to life when God's breath entered them.
What is sown in weakness is raised in power: we believe in the resurrection of the body.
Praying for the dead is a work of mercy; the Holy Qurbana is the greatest help we can give them.
2027-02-05.action: Pray by name today for each of your departed family members.
2027-02-05.question: Do I remember my dead before God, or only in memory?

family.explain: God showed the prophet Ezekiel a valley full of dry bones. When God breathed on them, they came to life and stood up! God promises that he will raise our dear ones who have died, and give them new life.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all our family members who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we make a list of our family members who have died and pray for them together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Changanassery the young people of the family union noticed some old graves in the cemetery that no one visited any more; the families had moved away or died out. On the Friday of the Faithful Departed they cleaned those graves, lit candles on them, and asked the parish priest to pray the oppees there too. An old woman watching said: now no one in this cemetery is forgotten.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, resurrection and life, we gather in communion with all who have gone before us. Breathe your Spirit upon us and upon them. Amen.
share: Mortal, can these bones live? (Ezekiel 37:3). Is there anything in me that feels dry and dead?
Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives on (Sirach 44:14). Whom do I remember before God?
Just as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me (Matthew 25:40). Whom have I served, and whom have I passed by?
pm.resp: Eternal rest grant to them, O Lord.
interc: For all the faithful departed, especially our families and benefactors.
For those who have no one to pray for them.
For those who are dying today.
For the grieving and the lonely.
For our group, that we may serve Christ in the least.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the first fruits of those who have died. Grant eternal rest to all the departed, and bring us all together into your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Laodiceans were lukewarm and said: we need nothing.
Christ stands at the door and knocks; if we open, he will come in and eat with us.
The crowds laid their sick at Jesus' feet, and he cured them.
2027-02-06.action: Make or plan a good confession before the Great Fast begins.
2027-02-06.question: Is there any area where I say to God: I need nothing?

family.explain: Jesus says: I am standing at your door, knocking. If you open, I will come in and eat with you! Many people brought sick friends to Jesus, and he healed them all.
family.intention: We pray for the sick, and for a good beginning of the Great Fast.
family.ask: Ask: “What will our family do for Jesus in this Great Fast?”

illus: An illustration

A young professional in Kochi, successful and busy, went to the Holy Qurbana only at Christmas and Easter. When a friend asked if he prayed, he laughed: I have everything I need. A few months later his company closed and his father fell ill in the same week. Sitting late at night in the hospital corridor, he found himself reading the words on a picture on the wall: I am standing at the door, knocking. He said later: I had kept the door locked because I thought I was rich. That night I opened it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stand at the door and knock. We open the door to you; come in and stay with us. Amen.
share: Because you are lukewarm, I am about to spit you out of my mouth (Revelation 3:16). Where am I lukewarm?
If you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in (Revelation 3:20). What keeps my door closed?
They put them at his feet, and he cured them (Matthew 15:30). Whom will I bring to Jesus' feet?
pm.resp: Lord, come in and stay with us.
interc: For the whole Church, that the Great Fast may be a time of true conversion.
For those who are lukewarm or have drifted away.
For the sick and the disabled.
For those who think they need nothing.
For our group, that we may open the door to Christ.
pm.close: Father, your Son knocks at our door and heals all who are laid at his feet. Prepare us for the Great Fast with humble and open hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Great Fast begins: we are dust, and God is our life.
God says again, “Let there be light”; the fast is a new creation.
First be reconciled, then offer your gift.
2027-02-08.action: Take the first step of reconciliation with one person today.
2027-02-08.question: Who has something against me, and what is my first step?

family.explain: Jesus says: if you come to church with a gift for God and remember that your brother is upset with you, leave the gift, go and make peace first, and then come back. God wants our hearts at peace with one another before we pray together.
family.intention: We pray for families where people are not speaking to one another.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone in our family to whom we need to say sorry today?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers near Pala had not spoken for six years because of a boundary wall between their plots. On the morning of the Vibhoodi the younger one stood in the line for the ashes and found himself just behind his elder brother. When the priest said the words about dust, he thought: our wall will outlast both of us. After the service he walked over and said only, come home for tea. The wall is still there, but the gate in it is open now.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we begin the Great Fast before you. Make us dust that is open to your breath. Amen.
share: Let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Where do I need God's light this Lent?
Be strong and courageous (Joshua 1:9). What crossing lies before me in these seven weeks?
First be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). With whom must I make peace?
pm.resp: Lord, create a new heart in us.
interc: For the whole Church as she begins the Great Fast.
For all who are estranged from their families.
For the poor, who will receive what our fast saves.
For those who find fasting difficult because of illness or age.
For our group, that we may keep this fast with joy.
pm.close: Father, you call us back to you with fasting and prayer. Reconcile us with you and with one another, and lead us through these days to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God made us from dust and breathed his life into us.
God's kindness is meant to lead us to repentance.
Jesus asks us to walk the second mile.
2027-02-09.action: Put aside today the money your fast saves, in a box for the poor.
2027-02-09.question: Do I take God's kindness for granted?

family.explain: Jesus says: if someone is unkind to you, do not hit back. If someone asks you to walk one mile with him, walk two! Jesus wants us to be more generous than anyone expects, because God is so generous with us.
family.intention: We pray for people who have hurt us.
family.ask: Ask: “What extra kindness can each of us do this week?”

illus: An illustration

An autorickshaw driver in Kochi was asked by an elderly passenger to wait while she collected her medicines, though she said she had no money to pay for the waiting. He waited, and then carried her bags up three flights of stairs. She asked his name so that she could pray for him. He smiled and said: it is the Great Fast, Ammachi; this is my second mile.

pm.open: Lord God, you formed us from the dust and gave us your breath. Breathe on us now as we pray. Amen.
share: The Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground (Genesis 2:7). What does it mean for me that I carry God's breath?
God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance (Romans 2:4). How has God's kindness called me back?
Go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). Where is God asking me to give more?
pm.resp: Lord, make us generous like you.
interc: For the Church, that she may show God's kindness to all.
For those who judge others harshly, and for those who are judged.
For the poor who depend on our generosity this Lent.
For those who have hurt us, and those we have hurt.
For our group, that we may walk the second mile together.
pm.close: Father, your kindness leads us to repentance. Make our fasting generous and our hearts patient, like your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: It is not good to be alone: we keep the fast as families.
Rahab believed and was saved; be a doer of the word.
Pray in secret; the Father sees and knows what you need.
2027-02-10.action: Pray for ten minutes today in a quiet room with the door shut.
2027-02-10.question: Do I pray to be seen, or to be with the Father?

family.explain: Jesus says: when you pray, you do not need to show off or use lots of words. Go to a quiet place, shut the door, and talk to your Father in heaven. He already knows what you need, and he loves to hear you!
family.intention: We pray for married couples and for families keeping the Great Fast together.
family.ask: Ask: “Where in our home can we make a quiet corner for prayer?”

illus: An illustration

A young couple in Kottayam, both working long shifts, agreed at the start of the Great Fast to switch off their phones at nine each night and pray together for ten minutes. The first evenings were awkward; the silence felt long. By Easter the wife said they had talked to each other more in those seven weeks than in the whole year before. The husband said: we went into the room to talk to God, and we found each other there too.

pm.open: Father in heaven, we have come into your presence. You see in secret and you know what we need. Hear us. Amen.
share: It is not good that the man should be alone (Genesis 2:18). How can my family keep this fast together?
The LORD your God is indeed God in heaven above and on earth below (Joshua 2:11). What does Rahab's faith teach me?
Pray to your Father who is in secret (Matthew 6:6). Do I have an inner room for prayer?
interc: For the Church in Kerala, of every tradition, walking through the Lenten season together.
For married couples, that they may pray together.
For those who are lonely, especially the elderly living alone.
For those who have never learned to pray.
For our group, that our prayer may be sincere.
pm.close: Father, you see in secret and know our needs before we ask. Draw us into prayer that is honest and simple, and bless our families in this holy fast. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Sin began with suspicion; God still asks: where are you?
God goes before us like the ark into the river.
Strive first for the kingdom; the Father knows what you need.
2027-02-11.action: Write down your biggest worry and hand it to God in prayer.
2027-02-11.question: Where am I hiding from God?

family.explain: Jesus says: look at the birds. They do not have kitchens or shops, but God feeds them. Look at the flowers. They do not sew clothes, but God makes them beautiful. You are worth much more to God than birds and flowers! So do not worry. Put God first.
family.intention: We pray for sick people and for those who care for them.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we are worried about? Let us give it to God together.”

illus: An illustration

A mother in Thodupuzha lay awake every night worrying about her son working in the Gulf. At the start of the Great Fast she began a small practice: each night she wrote her worry on a slip of paper and dropped it into a box placed before the image of Our Lady. By Easter the box was full. She laughed and told her neighbour: I gave the box the night shift. My son still has problems, but now I sleep, and I pray better in the morning.

pm.open: Lord God, you call us by name: where are you? Here we are, Lord. Amen.
share: Where are you? (Genesis 3:9). Where am I hiding from God?
Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you (Joshua 3:5). How am I preparing for what God wants to do?
Strive first for the kingdom of God (Matthew 6:33). What comes first in my life?
pm.resp: Lord, we trust in your care.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim God's providence.
For the sick, through the prayers of Our Lady of Lourdes.
For doctors, nurses and caregivers.
For those overwhelmed by worry about money, work or children.
For our group, that we may seek first the kingdom.
pm.close: Father, you feed the birds and clothe the lilies. Free us from anxiety, forgive our hiding, and teach us to seek your kingdom first. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God asks: where is your brother? We are our brothers' keepers.
Abraham hoped against hope and believed God's promise.
First take the log out of your own eye.
2027-02-12.action: Walk the Way of the Cross today, at church or at home.
2027-02-12.question: Whom do I judge, and what is the log in my own eye?

family.explain: Cain was jealous of his brother Abel and hurt him very badly. God asked Cain: where is your brother? Cain said: I do not know; am I my brother's keeper? But God wants us to look after one another. Every brother and sister is a gift from God.
family.intention: We pray for brothers and sisters who are quarrelling.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we look after each other better in our family?”

illus: An illustration

A man in Alappuzha used to criticise his neighbour's drinking at every parish gathering. One Lenten Friday, at the station where Jesus falls the third time, he suddenly remembered his own temper at home, and how his children went quiet when he came in. That evening he went to his neighbour's house, not to preach, but to ask him to walk the Way of the Cross with him the next Friday. The neighbour came. Both of them, the man said later, had logs to carry.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this Friday of the Great Fast we stand before your Cross. Look on us with mercy. Amen.
share: Where is your brother Abel? (Genesis 4:9). Whom am I neglecting?
Hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). Where do I need Abraham's faith?
First take the log out of your own eye (Matthew 7:5). What do I need to see in myself?
interc: For the Church as she walks the Way of the Cross this Friday.
For victims of violence and for those who have killed.
For brothers and sisters divided by jealousy or property.
For those who have lost hope.
For our group, that we may stop judging one another.
pm.close: Father, the blood of your Son speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Make us keepers of one another and give us the faith of Abraham. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: All have sinned; we are justified by grace as a gift.
The Our Father is the programme of the Great Fast.
The forgiven must forgive.
2027-02-13.action: Pray the Our Father slowly, a minute on each line.
2027-02-13.question: Do I fast with gratitude or with pride?

family.explain: Jesus taught his friends a prayer: the Our Father. We call God our Father, we ask him for our bread each day, and we ask him to forgive us, just as we forgive others. Jesus says this is very important: if we forgive, God forgives us.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who finds it hard to forgive.
family.ask: Ask: “Can we pray the Our Father together slowly tonight, and think about each line?”

illus: An illustration

A catechism teacher in Irinjalakuda asked her class to pray the Our Father aloud, pausing after the words about forgiving others. One boy fell silent at that line. Afterwards he told her he could not say it, because he was angry with his cousin. The next Sunday he came early and whispered: we made up yesterday. Now I can say the whole prayer.

pm.open: Our Father in heaven, we come to you as your children, justified by your grace. Hallowed be your name. Amen.
share: They are now justified by his grace as a gift (Romans 3:24). Do I receive God's love as a gift, or try to earn it?
Give us this day our daily bread (Matthew 6:11). What does fasting teach me about this petition?
If you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). Whom must I forgive?
pm.resp: Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the free gift of God's grace.
For those who carry old wounds and cannot forgive.
For those who have no daily bread.
For those in the time of trial and temptation.
For our group, that we may pray the Our Father with sincere hearts.
pm.close: Father, you justify us freely in your Son. Teach us to pray as he taught us, and to forgive as we have been forgiven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the Lord enters his Temple. Forty days after his birth, Mary and Joseph bring him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, as the law commanded, and they offer a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons (Luke 2:24). It was the offering of the poor.

The law of Leviticus said that a mother who could not afford a lamb could bring two birds. But on that day the true Lamb was in his mother's arms. The poor offering was made for the One who would offer himself for the whole world.

Simeon, righteous and devout, has waited all his life. Guided by the Spirit he comes into the Temple, takes the child in his arms and says: master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:29–30).

Then he tells Mary that this child will be a sign that will be opposed, and that a sword will pierce her soul. Paul, in the Epistle, grieves that many stumbled over this stone. Yet Christ is the end of the law, so that there may be righteousness for everyone who believes (Romans 10:4).

Anna, eighty-four years old, worships night and day with fasting and prayer, and speaks about the child to all who are waiting. Isaiah had promised a Servant who would be a light to the nations. Simeon and Anna see that light in a baby.

On this World Day for Consecrated Life let us thank God for our religious sisters, brothers and priests, presented to God like the child in the Temple. And let us keep awake, like Simeon and Anna, so that when the Lord comes we may recognize him and say: my eyes have seen your salvation. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was a tiny baby, Mary and Joseph took him to the Temple to give him to God. Old Simeon held him and was so happy!
Each morning you can also say: Jesus, I give you my day!

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we enter the Great Fast. Moses was with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water (Exodus 34:28). When he came down, his face shone because he had been talking with God, and he did not even know it.
This is the purpose of the fast: not first to lose weight or to suffer, but to be with God, so that his light may begin to shine in us.

Isaiah warns that a fast can be empty. People fasted and quarrelled, fasted and oppressed their workers. God says: is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to share your bread with the hungry? (Isaiah 58:6–7). Then your light shall break forth like the dawn.

Paul tells us to put away the old self and clothe ourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God (Ephesians 4:22–24). The Great Fast is a change of clothes: the old self off, Christ on.

In the Gospel Jesus fasts forty days and is tempted three times: bread, a spectacle, power. Each time he answers with the word of God: one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God (Matthew 4:4). Where Adam and Israel failed, he stands firm.

We fast in him, and his victory is ours. Tonight, at Pethurtha, let us forgive one another at home. From tomorrow let us pray more, eat less, give more, and feed on God's word, so that at Easter our faces too may shine. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus did not eat for forty days, and when the devil tempted him, he said: God's word is more important than bread!
In the Great Fast, give up one sweet thing and say one extra prayer each day.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the first reading is a long list of names, and after almost every name the same words: and he died. But one man is different: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him (Genesis 5:24). He walked with God while raising sons and daughters, in an ordinary home.
That is the goal of the Great Fast. Not simply to give up fish and meat, but to walk with God, day after day, in our homes and at our work.

Israel crossed the Jordan and set up twelve stones, so that when the children asked, what do these stones mean?, the parents would tell them the story of God's mighty hand (Joshua 4:21–22). Our Lenten customs are such stones. When our children ask why we fast, let us tell them about Jesus.
Paul reminds us that everyone serves someone. For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord (Romans 6:23). Sin pays wages; God gives gifts.

Jesus warns us: not everyone who says to me, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father (Matthew 7:21). The two houses face the same storm. The difference is the foundation: the one who hears and acts has built on rock.
This week, let us choose one word of Jesus and do it. Let us dig down to the rock while the sky is clear. Then, when the storms come, our house will stand. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about a house on the rock and a house on the sand. When the rain came, only the house on the rock stood strong!
When we listen to Jesus and do what he says, we are building on the rock. What will you do this week?

homily: Dear friends, Paul asks the Thessalonians to pray that the word of the Lord may spread, because not all have faith. Then he adds: but the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one (2 Thessalonians 3:3).

In the Gospel a woman who has been ill for twelve years comes up behind Jesus. She thinks: if I only touch his cloak, I will be made well (Matthew 9:21). Jesus turns, looks at her and says: take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.
Then he goes to the house of the synagogue leader, whose daughter has died. The mourners laugh when he says she is sleeping. But he takes her by the hand, and the girl gets up.
Our faith may be as small as a touch. It is enough, because the one we touch is faithful. Let us reach out to him today, and let him direct our hearts to the love of God. Amen.
kids: Children, a sick lady touched just the edge of Jesus' clothes, and she was healed! Jesus loves it when we come to him with trust. What will you ask Jesus today?

homily: Dear friends, Paul charges Timothy: proclaim the message; be persistent whether the time is favorable or unfavorable (2 Timothy 4:2). People will look for teachers who say what their itching ears want to hear. But Timothy must do the work of an evangelist.
In the Gospel the Samaritan woman leaves her water jar and runs back to the city: come and see a man who told me everything I have ever done! She came for water and found the Messiah.
The disciples urge Jesus to eat. He says: my food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work (John 4:34). Then he shows them the fields ripe for harvesting.
We reap what others have sown: the apostle Thomas, our missionaries, our parents and catechists. Let us thank them, leave our water jars, and say to someone: come and see. Amen.
kids: Children, a lady met Jesus at a well and was so happy that she forgot her water jar! She ran to tell everyone: come and see Jesus! Who can you tell about Jesus today?

homily: Dear friends, Peter tells us: regard the patience of our Lord as salvation (2 Peter 3:15). Every day that God waits is a day of mercy, given so that we may grow in the grace and knowledge of Christ.

Jesus asks us to show others the same patience: do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven (Luke 6:37). The measure we give is the measure we get back.
Then he gives us a picture: someone with a log in his own eye trying to take a speck out of his neighbour's eye. First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly.

St John de Britto left the royal court of Portugal to live like a poor Tamil ascetic. He became all things to all people, and in 1693 he gave his life at Oriyur. May we, too, judge less, love more, and give ourselves in good measure. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a funny story about a man with a big log in his eye who wanted to take a tiny speck from his friend's eye! Let us look at our own faults first, and be kind to others.

homily: Dear friends, today, on the last Friday of Denha, we remember all the faithful departed. Ezekiel sees a valley full of dry bones, and God asks: mortal, can these bones live? (Ezekiel 37:3). When God's breath enters them, they live and stand up, a vast multitude.
Sirach praises our ancestors, the famous and the forgotten. Their bodies are buried in peace, but their name lives on generation after generation (Sirach 44:14). God has forgotten none of them.

Paul tells us that the body is like a seed: it is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory; it is sown in weakness, it is raised in power (1 Corinthians 15:43). We bury our dead in hope, because we believe in the resurrection of the body.

In the Gospel the King says: just as you did it to one of the least of these, you did it to me (Matthew 25:40). Let us serve Christ in the poor, pray for our departed, have the Holy Qurbana offered for them, and so prepare for the Great Fast that begins this Sunday. Amen.
kids: Children, God showed Ezekiel dry bones that came to life again! God will raise up our grandparents and everyone who loved him. Tonight, let us pray for our family members who have died.

homily: Dear friends, the risen Christ writes to the church of Laodicea: I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot (Revelation 3:15). They were rich and said: we need nothing. But they did not see that they were poor, blind and naked.

His words are hard, but they come from love: I reprove and discipline those whom I love. And then: listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you (Revelation 3:20).
In the Gospel great crowds bring the lame, the maimed, the blind and the mute and put them at Jesus' feet, and he cures them all. They did not pretend to be rich. They brought their poverty to him.
Tomorrow the Great Fast begins. Let us not be lukewarm. Let us admit our need, open the door with a good confession, and lay ourselves at his feet. Then he will come in and eat with us. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: I am knocking at your door! When we pray and say sorry for our sins, we open the door, and Jesus comes in to be our friend. Will you open the door for Jesus?

homily: Dear friends, this morning the ash has marked our foreheads. The words remind us of the first sin and its sentence: you are dust, and to dust you shall return (Genesis 3:19). Yesterday was Pethurtha; the feasting is over, and the fifty days fast has begun.

But the Church gives us today the first page of the Bible. God speaks into the darkness: let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Again and again he looks at what he has made and sees that it is good. The fast does not despise God's gifts. It makes room for God to create us anew.

Like Joshua at the Jordan, we stand at the edge of a crossing. God says to us too: be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go (Joshua 1:9). And he gives us his word to carry, to meditate on day and night.

Jesus goes to the heart of the matter: if you remember at the altar that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there and go; first be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). Let the ash on our foreheads lead to peace in our homes. Then our fast will be pleasing to God. Amen.
kids: Children, today the priest put ash on our foreheads in the shape of a cross. It means: I belong to Jesus, and I want to start again. Is there someone you need to say sorry to today?

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we heard that we are dust. Today Genesis tells us what God does with dust: the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life (Genesis 2:7). We are dust, and we carry God's breath and image.

Paul warns us against judging others, because the judge is often doing the very same things. And he asks: do you not realize that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance? (Romans 2:4). God has been patient with us. That patience is an invitation to come home.

Jesus asks us to pass on that kindness: turn the other cheek; give your cloak as well; if anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile (Matthew 5:41). This is not weakness. It is the strength of love that does not answer evil with evil.
Let our fast become generous. What we save by fasting, let us give to the poor. And let us walk the second mile with someone who is difficult. Then God's image will shine in us again. Amen.
kids: Children, God made us from dust and breathed his own life into us. That is why every person is precious! Today, do one extra kind thing that nobody asked you to do.

homily: Dear friends, the first thing in creation that God calls not good is loneliness: it is not good that the man should be alone (Genesis 2:18). So God gives the man a partner, and the two become one flesh. We do not keep the Great Fast alone. We keep it as families, as a parish, as one Church.

Rahab, a woman of Jericho, hears what God has done and believes: the LORD your God is indeed God in heaven above and on earth below (Joshua 2:11). She ties a crimson cord in her window and is saved with her family. Paul reminds us that God wants doers of his word, not only hearers.

And Jesus teaches us how to pray: not to be seen, not with many words, but in the inner room. Go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret (Matthew 6:6). The Father knows what we need before we ask.
This Great Fast, let us find our inner room, and let our families pray together each evening. Then the Father who sees in secret will reward us. Amen.
kids: Children, you can talk to God anywhere, even in a quiet corner of your room. Shut the door, close your eyes and tell him what is in your heart. He is listening!

homily: Dear friends, the first sin began with a suspicion: that God was holding something back. Adam and Eve ate, their eyes were opened, and they hid. Then God came looking: where are you? (Genesis 3:9). He still asks that question, not to shame us, but to call us out of hiding.

Adam blamed the woman, and the woman blamed the serpent. Paul says that no one is righteous, not even one. The Great Fast begins when we stop blaming and say honestly: Lord, here I am, a sinner in need of you.

Joshua tells the people: sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you (Joshua 3:5). The ark of God goes first into the river. And Jesus tells us not to worry about food and clothing: look at the birds of the air; consider the lilies of the field.

When we fast we eat less, and we find that the Father still feeds us. So let us strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to us as well (Matthew 6:33). Amen.
kids: Children, God feeds the little birds and dresses the flowers in beautiful colours. He loves you even more! When you are worried, tell Jesus about it and trust him.

homily: Dear friends, God asked Adam: where are you? Today he asks Cain: where is your brother Abel? (Genesis 4:9). Sin against God soon becomes sin against the brother. Cain answers: am I my brother's keeper? God's answer is yes.

God had warned Cain: sin is lurking at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it (Genesis 4:7). Jealousy began with comparing. That is why Jesus says: do not judge. First take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly (Matthew 7:5).
Abraham teaches us another way: hoping against hope, he believed (Romans 4:18). He did not look at his weakness but at God's promise. And Israel crossed the Jordan because God held back the waters.

Today is a Friday of the Great Fast. As we walk the Way of the Cross, we see the blood of Jesus, which speaks a better word than the blood of Abel. Let us become keepers of our brothers and sisters. Amen.
kids: Children, God asks each of us: where is your brother? where is your sister? Jesus wants us to take care of each other. Do something kind for your brother, sister or friend today.

homily: Dear friends, Paul says that all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God; they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus (Romans 3:23–24). Our fasting does not buy God's love. His love comes first.
So we fast with gratitude, not with pride. Our prayer, fasting and almsgiving are our answer to a gift already given, and God's grace makes even that answer possible.

Jesus gives us the prayer of the whole Great Fast: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name (Matthew 6:9). We pray it at the beginning of the Holy Qurbana and again before Communion. In it we ask for daily bread, for forgiveness, and for rescue in the time of trial.

Jesus explains one line only: if you forgive others, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). As this first week of the fast ends, let us forgive from the heart, so that we can pray this prayer honestly. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus taught us to call God our Father! Tonight, pray the Our Father slowly with your family, and think of someone you need to forgive.

intro: Theme: “My eyes have seen your salvation.”
Mayaltho: the Lord enters his Temple, presented with the offering of the poor and received by those who waited.

q: Consecrate to me all the firstborn; whatever is the first to open the womb among the Israelites, of human beings and animals, is mine.
When the time came for their purification according to the law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord
points.apply: Offer yourself and your family to God at the start of each day.

sub: Light for the Gentiles, light for India.
q: I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, I have taken you by the hand and kept you; I have given you as a covenant to the people, a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.

Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace, according to your word; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.
points.apply: Be gentle this week with someone who is bruised and weak.

points.h: A sign that will be opposed
sub: Christ, the end of the law.
q: See, I am laying in Zion a foundation stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation: “One who trusts will not panic.”

Then Simeon blessed them and said to his mother Mary, “This child is destined for the falling and the rising of many in Israel, and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed—and a sword will pierce your own soul too.”
points.apply: When following Christ brings opposition, unite your pain with Mary's.

points.h: Fasting and prayer night and day
sub: The Lord comes to his temple.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.

She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day. At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
points.apply: Spend some quiet time before the Blessed Sacrament this week, waiting on the Lord.

concl: The Lord of the Temple came as a poor child, and only those who waited recognized him.
Keep awake with Simeon and Anna, and you too will see his salvation.
2027-02-02.resolve: Pray this week for consecrated persons, and thank one of them personally.

intro: Theme: “One does not live by bread alone.”
The Great Fast begins: forty days with God, the fast God chooses, victory over temptation, and the new self.

q: He was there with the LORD forty days and forty nights; he neither ate bread nor drank water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten commandments.

And all of us, with unveiled faces, seeing the glory of the Lord as though reflected in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another; for this comes from the Lord, the Spirit.
points.apply: Set a fixed time of prayer every day of the Great Fast.

q: He humbled you by letting you hunger, then by feeding you with manna, with which neither you nor your ancestors were acquainted, in order to make you understand that one does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
But he answered, “It is written, ‘One does not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
points.apply: Read one chapter of a Gospel every day of the Great Fast.

q: Is not this the fast that I choose: to loose the bonds of injustice, to undo the thongs of the yoke, to let the oppressed go free, and to break every yoke? Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
How does God's love abide in anyone who has the world's goods and sees a brother or sister in need and yet refuses help?
points.apply: Keep a box for what you save by fasting, and give it to the poor at Easter.

q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.

You were taught to put away your former way of life, your old self, corrupt and deluded by its lusts, and to be renewed in the spirit of your minds, and to clothe yourselves with the new self, created according to the likeness of God in true righteousness and holiness.
points.apply: Name one habit of the old self to put away during these fifty days.

concl: The Great Fast is time with God, a fast of justice and sharing, and a change of clothes.
In Christ who overcame the tempter, we too can overcome.
2027-02-07.resolve: Be reconciled tonight at Pethurtha, and begin the fast tomorrow with prayer, fasting and almsgiving.

intro: Theme: “Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.”
Enoch who walked with God, the stones of the Jordan, the free gift of God, and the house built on rock.

q: Enoch walked with God; then he was no more, because God took him.
By faith Enoch was taken so that he did not experience death; and “he was not found, because God had taken him.” For it was attested before he was taken away that “he had pleased God.”
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes each day this week walking with God in prayer.

sub: Our Lenten customs tell Christ's story.
q: so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is mighty, and so that you may fear the LORD your God forever.”
like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Explain to a child this week the meaning of one Lenten custom of your family.

sub: Slaves of sin or of God.
The free gift of eternal life.
q: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live,
For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
points.apply: Make your Lenten confession before the third Sunday of the Great Fast.

sub: Not everyone who says Lord, Lord.
The same storm for both houses.
Digging while the sky is clear.
q: The LORD is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, my God, my rock in whom I take refuge, my shield, and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold.
“Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
points.apply: Choose one word of the Sermon on the Mount and live it daily this week.

concl: The Great Fast is not a list of things given up but a walk with God, remembered and handed on.
Choose the gift, do the word, and build on the rock while the sky is clear.
2027-02-14.resolve: Put one teaching of Jesus into practice every day this week, and explain the meaning of the fast to a child.

intro: Theme: “But the Lord is faithful.”
The faithful Lord, the woman who reached out, and the girl raised by the hand.

q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
But the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.
points.apply: Thank God each morning this week for one sign of his faithfulness.

points.h: If I only touch his cloak
q: Bless the LORD, O my soul, and do not forget all his benefits— who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,
Jesus turned, and seeing her he said, “Take heart, daughter; your faith has made you well.” And instantly the woman was made well.
points.apply: Bring one long-standing trouble to Jesus in prayer today.

sub: He takes her by the hand.
q: Your dead shall live, their corpses shall rise. O dwellers in the dust, awake and sing for joy!
But when the crowd had been put outside, he went in and took her by the hand, and the girl got up.
points.apply: Pray for a family that has lost a child or a young person.

concl: Our faith may be small, but the Lord is faithful.
Reach out and touch him; he turns, and he raises up.
2027-02-01.resolve: Each day this week, make one short act of trust in the Lord's faithfulness.

intro: Theme: “My food is to do the will of him who sent me.”
The apostle's last charge, the woman who left her water jar, and the harvest that others sowed.

points.h: My food is to do his will
sub: Food you do not know about.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
Jesus said to them, “My food is to do the will of him who sent me and to complete his work.
points.apply: Begin today by asking: Father, what is your will for me today?

q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
Do you not say, ‘Four months more, then comes the harvest’? But I tell you, look around you, and see how the fields are ripe for harvesting.
points.apply: Invite one person who has drifted away to come with you to the Holy Qurbana.

sub: In season and out of season.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
proclaim the message; be persistent whether the time is favorable or unfavorable; convince, rebuke, and encourage, with the utmost patience in teaching.
points.apply: Speak a word of faith this week where you would usually stay silent.

concl: Christ is fed by the Father's will, and he feeds us so that we may do it too.
Leave your water jar, look at the fields, and proclaim him.
2027-02-03.resolve: Thank and pray for those who first taught you the faith, and share it with one person this week.

intro: Theme: “Forgive, and you will be forgiven.”
God's patience, the log in our own eye, and the martyr who became all things to all people.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
Do not judge, and you will not be judged; do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven;
points.apply: Forgive one person today, in your heart and, if possible, in words.

points.h: The log in my own eye
q: Search me, O God, and know my heart; test me and know my thoughts. See if there is any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your neighbor's eye.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience tonight before you sleep.

sub: A Portuguese courtier turned Tamil ascetic.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
To the weak I became weak, so that I might win the weak. I have become all things to all people, that I might by all means save some.
points.apply: Learn a greeting or a prayer in the language of a neighbour or co-worker.

concl: God's patience with us is the measure of our patience with others.
Take out your own log, and love others as the saints did, in good measure.
2027-02-04.resolve: Go one day this week without criticizing anyone, and pray for missionaries.

intro: Theme: “It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory.”
The valley of dry bones, the resurrection of the body, and the mercy of praying for the dead.

q: He said to me, “Mortal, can these bones live?” I answered, “O Lord GOD, you know.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live,
points.apply: Bring to God one area of your life that feels dry and dead.

sub: Like a seed in the earth.
The man of dust and the man of heaven.
q: Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.
So it is with the resurrection of the dead. What is sown is perishable, what is raised is imperishable. It is sown in dishonor, it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness, it is raised in power.
points.apply: Visit the cemetery this week and pray with hope at the graves.

q: But if he was looking to the splendid reward that is laid up for those who fall asleep in godliness, it was a holy and pious thought. Therefore he made atonement for the dead, so that they might be delivered from their sin.
And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.’
points.apply: Have a Holy Qurbana offered for your departed, and give an alms in their name.

concl: God has forgotten none of our dead; he will raise them in glory.
Pray for them, serve Christ in the least, and enter the Great Fast in hope.
2027-02-05.resolve: Make a list of your departed family members and pray for them every day of the Great Fast.

intro: Theme: “I am standing at the door, knocking.”
The lukewarm church, the Lord who knocks, and the crowds who laid their poverty at his feet.

q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
I know your works; you are neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were either cold or hot.
points.apply: Name one area where you have grown lukewarm, and choose one act of fervour for the Great Fast.

sub: He does not break the door.
He wants to eat with us.
q: I slept, but my heart was awake. Listen! my beloved is knocking. “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my perfect one;
Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.
points.apply: Open the door with a good confession before or early in the Great Fast.

sub: The lame, the blind, the mute.
They praised the God of Israel.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
Great crowds came to him, bringing with them the lame, the maimed, the blind, the mute, and many others. They put them at his feet, and he cured them,
points.apply: Bring a sick or disabled person to Jesus in prayer, and visit them this week.

concl: Christ knocks at the door of every lukewarm heart.
Admit your poverty, open the door, and let him carry you into the Great Fast.
2027-02-06.resolve: Begin the Great Fast with a good confession and one concrete act of fervour.

intro: Theme: “first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.”
The ash of the Vibhoodi, the first light of creation, Joshua's courage, and the peace Jesus asks before the altar.

q: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; you are dust, and to dust you shall return.
For he says, “At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.” See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Write down today what you will fast from, and keep the note in your Bible.

sub: God saw that it was good.
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
points.apply: Ask God each morning of this week to speak his light into one dark corner of your life.

sub: The gift left at the altar.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
points.apply: Take the first step towards one estranged person before Sunday.

concl: The Great Fast begins with ash and with light: we are dust, and God speaks over us again.
Be strong and courageous, and let the first fruit of the fast be peace.
2027-02-08.resolve: Make peace with one person before receiving Holy Qurbana on Sunday.

intro: Theme: “God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance.”
Dust that carries God's breath, the patience of God, and the generosity of the second mile.

sub: Renewed in the image of the Creator.
q: then the Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and the man became a living being.
and have clothed yourselves with the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge according to the image of its creator.
points.apply: Thank God today for your body and your life, and offer both to him in the fast.

q: rend your hearts and not your clothing. Return to the LORD, your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love, and relents from punishing.
Or do you despise the riches of his kindness and forbearance and patience? Do you not realize that God's kindness is meant to lead you to repentance?
points.apply: Replace one judgment of another person with a prayer for them.

sub: Not an eye for an eye.
What the fast saves, the poor receive.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
and if anyone forces you to go one mile, go also the second mile.
points.apply: Give away this week what your fast has saved.

concl: We are dust, but dust that carries God's breath, and God's kindness calls us home.
Let that kindness flow through us, one second mile at a time.
2027-02-09.resolve: Keep a box for the poor at home through the whole Great Fast.

intro: Theme: “Your Father who sees in secret will reward you.”
The gift of companionship, Rahab's faith, and the inner room of prayer.

q: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
points.apply: Plan with your family one shared Lenten practice and keep it until Easter.

points.h: A crimson cord in the window
q: She said, “According to your words, so be it.” She sent them away and they departed. Then she tied the crimson cord in the window.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.
points.apply: Put into practice today one word of Scripture you already know well.

q: O LORD, you have searched me and known me.
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Make a quiet prayer corner at home this week.

concl: God made us for communion: with one another, and above all with him.
Keep the fast together, live the word you hear, and meet the Father in secret.
2027-02-10.resolve: Pray ten minutes in silence every day of this week.

intro: Theme: “But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness.”
God's question in the garden, the ark that goes ahead into the river, and the trust that fasting teaches.

q: But the Lord God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”
For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.
points.apply: Make a careful examination of conscience tonight and plan your Lenten confession.

q: Then Joshua said to the people, “Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you.”
Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.
points.apply: Choose one habit to give up this Lent as preparation for what God will do.

q: Cast your burden on the LORD, and he will sustain you; he will never permit the righteous to be moved.
But strive first for the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be given to you as well.
points.apply: Each morning this week, name one worry and hand it to God before you begin work.

concl: God calls us out of hiding and goes ahead of us into the river.
Let the fast teach us to trust: the Father knows what we need.
2027-02-11.resolve: Go to confession during the first weeks of the Great Fast.

intro: Theme: “Where is your brother Abel?”
Cain's question, Abraham's hope, the stones of the Jordan, and the eye that judges.

sub: A better word from the Cross.
q: Then the Lord said to Cain, “Where is your brother Abel?” He said, “I do not know; am I my brother's keeper?”
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars; for those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.
points.apply: Do one concrete thing this week for a brother, sister or neighbour in need.

sub: A body as good as dead.
q: And he believed the LORD; and the LORD reckoned it to him as righteousness.
Hoping against hope, he believed that he would become “the father of many nations,” according to what was said, “So numerous shall your descendants be.”
points.apply: Bring one hopeless situation to God every day of this week.

q: For I know my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me.
You hypocrite, first take the log out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your neighbor's eye.
points.apply: Each time you are tempted to criticise someone today, name one of your own faults instead.

concl: God asks where our brother is, and the Cross answers with mercy.
Keep your brother, hope against hope, and let Christ heal your eyes.
2027-02-12.resolve: Walk the Way of the Cross on every Friday of the Great Fast.

intro: Theme: “And forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.”
Grace given freely, the prayer Christ taught, and the forgiveness that the forgiven must give.

q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
they are now justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus,
points.apply: Thank God today for one grace you know you did not earn.

sub: Daily bread for those who fast.
Rescue in the time of trial.
q: Yet, O LORD, you are our Father; we are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
“Pray then in this way: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name.
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly each night of the coming week.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
points.apply: Forgive one person by name before receiving Holy Qurbana tomorrow.

concl: The fast begins and ends in grace: God gives first, and we answer with gratitude.
Pray as Jesus taught, and forgive as you have been forgiven.
2027-02-13.resolve: Pray the Our Father slowly with your family every night until Easter.
